title: Point realization commutes with condensed coefficient extension
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $E_s^c$ and $U_s$ be the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], with the map $E_s^c\to U_s$ of [def-sfb-subfield-to-qlbar-coefficient-map]. Let $J_s$ be the rational adic-to-condensed realization of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] and $T^s_{E,\Omega}=U_s\otimes^L_{E_s^c}-$ the derived extension of [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar]. Over $s$, the integral category on which $J_s$ is built is the same full subcategory, with the same completed ring sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_s$ and the same morphisms, as $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]; hence $J_s$ is defined on its raw rationalization $D^b_c(s,E)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], with no further transport. On the rational adic category $D^b_c(s,E)$ there is a specified natural isomorphism of functors
$$\beta:T^s_{E,\Omega}\circ J_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_{E,s}\circ\operatorname{Fib}_s,$$
where $\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,E)\simeq D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ is the point equivalence of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] and $\rho_{E,s}$ is the finite-matrix condensed realization of [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace]. Its normalization is as follows. For $N\in D^b_c(s,E)$, choose a bounded finite-dimensional complex $C$ representing $\operatorname{Fib}_sN$. The realization of a quasi-inverse point representative of $C$ is identified termwise with $U_s^{\oplus\dim_E C^i}$, with differentials and chain maps the matrices of $C$ through $E\to\Omega$; $\beta_N$ is this identification combined with the point-equivalence unit. It is independent of bases and quasi-isomorphic representatives, natural on derived morphisms, and compatible with shifts. At the rational coefficient unit $E_s$ it is the canonical unit identification $T^s_{E,\Omega}J_s(E_s)\cong U_s=\rho_{E,s}(E[0])$. In particular its argument is the adic object $N$, while its right side is the realization of the vector-space complex $\operatorname{Fib}_sN$.

source.place: First sentence, factorization over Q_l. Agent-formulated missing point comparison between the specified J and the finite-matrix realization. Bhatt–Scholze 6.8.14(1)(2) and 6.8.15 give coefficient-category background but do not assert this comparison.

proof.text: Typing and choice of a lattice. The scheme $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is noetherian of dimension zero and $\ell$ is invertible on it because $\ell\ne p$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] applies: the integral category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] over $s$ and $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] are the same full subcategory of the derived category of modules over the same completed sheaf $A_s=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_s$. The rational category $\mathcal R_s(E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] and $D^b_c(s,E)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] are both the raw scalar localization of this category, with the same objects and $\operatorname{Hom}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$. They are therefore equal, and $J_s$ of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] is defined on $D^b_c(s,E)$. By [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], $\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,E)\to D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ is an exact equivalence commuting with shifts. Given $N$, choose a bounded complex $C$ of finite-dimensional $E$-spaces and an isomorphism $c_N:\operatorname{Fib}_sN\cong C$ in $D(E)$ [def-weil-point-fd-complexes]. Choose bases $(e^i_j)$ of the finitely many nonzero $C^i$. Let $a^i$ be the matrix of $d^i$, and choose $m\ge0$ with all entries of all $\varpi_E^ma^i$ in $\mathcal O_E$. In the rescaled bases $\varpi_E^{-mi}e^i_j$ the matrix of $d^i$ is $\varpi_E^ma^i$, since $d(\varpi_E^{-mi}e^i_j)=\varpi_E^m\sum_ka^i_{kj}\varpi_E^{-m(i+1)}e^{i+1}_k$. Thus their $\mathcal O_E$-spans form a bounded subcomplex $P\subset C$ of finite free $\mathcal O_E$-modules with $P\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E=C$. For $C=0$ take $P=0$.

source.place: First sentence, factorization over Q_l: compare the point realization after extension with the finite-dimensional E realization

proof.text: The point representative and the unit. Let $Q(P)$ be the complex of $A_s$-modules with terms $A_s^{\oplus\operatorname{rk}P^i}$ and differentials the integral matrices of $P$, acting through the constants $\mathcal O_E\to A_s$. On the single stratum $s$ it is $A_s\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}P$, since the terms are finite free. So it satisfies condition (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], and it lies in $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction], $A_s(V)=C(|V|,\mathcal O_E)$, so $\Gamma(s,A_s)=C(|s|,\mathcal O_E)=\mathcal O_E$, with constants going to constants. Since $s$ is the final object of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$, termwise sections give $\Gamma(s,Q(P))=P$. The definition of $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] (item 3: sections, then $\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$) gives $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Q(P))=P\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E=C$, with the identity as identification. By full faithfulness of $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], there is a unique isomorphism $u_N:N\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(P)$ in $D^b_c(s,E)$ with $\operatorname{Fib}_s(u_N)=c_N$.

source.place: First sentence, factorization over Q_l: compare the point realization after extension with the finite-dimensional E realization

proof.text: The termwise comparison. By [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization], $J_s$ is derived extension of scalars along $A_s\to E_s^c$. Under its canonical identification $E_s^c\cong(V\mapsto C(|V|,E))$ and [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction], this map is the inclusion $C(|V|,\mathcal O_E)\subset C(|V|,E)$. Here $E_s^c=p_s^*\underline E$ is the same construction in [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category] and [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The complex $Q(P)$ is bounded with finite free terms, hence K-flat, so the derived tensor is termwise. Thus $J_s(Q(P))$ has terms $(E_s^c)^{\oplus\dim C^i}$ and differentials the matrices $\varpi_E^ma^i$ through $E\to E_s^c$. The termwise diagonal isomorphism $\operatorname{diag}(\varpi_E^{-mi})$ (lattice coordinates to original coordinates; $\varpi_E^{-m(i+1)}\varpi_E^ma^i=a^i\varpi_E^{-mi}$) carries it to the complex with matrices $a^i$ of $C$ in the original bases. By [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar], $T^s_{E,\Omega}=U_s\otimes^L_{E_s^c}-$. By [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus], with $B=\Omega_s^c=U_s$, it is computed termwise on any representing complex. So $T^s_{E,\Omega}J_s(Q(P))$ has terms $U_s^{\oplus\dim C^i}$ and differentials $a^i$ through $E\to\Omega$. This is the finite-matrix complex $\rho_{E,s}(C)$ of [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace] in those bases. Call this identification $\kappa_P:T^s_{E,\Omega}J_s(Q(P))\cong\rho_{E,s}(C)$, and put $\beta_N=\rho_{E,s}(c_N)^{-1}\circ\kappa_P\circ T^s_{E,\Omega}J_s(u_N):T^s_{E,\Omega}J_s(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_{E,s}(\operatorname{Fib}_sN)$.

source.place: First sentence, factorization over Q_l: compare the point realization after extension with the finite-dimensional E realization

proof.text: Naturality and independence of choices. Let $f:N\to N'$ be a derived morphism, with choices $(C,c_N,P,u_N)$ and $(C',c_{N'},P',u_{N'})$; the case $N=N'$, $f=1$ with two sets of choices gives independence. The morphism $\varphi=c_{N'}\operatorname{Fib}_s(f)c_N^{-1}:C\to C'$ in $D(E)$ starts at a bounded complex of projective $E$-modules. By [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-lift] (with $\alpha$ the identity), it is the class of a chain map $\gamma:C\to C'$. Its matrices in the chosen lattice bases have entries in $\varpi_E^{-r}\mathcal O_E$ for some $r$. So $\varpi_E^r\gamma$ restricts to a chain map $P\to P'$, which induces a chain map $Q(\varpi_E^r\gamma):Q(P)\to Q(P')$. Put $g=\varpi_E^{-r}Q(\varpi_E^r\gamma)$ in $D^b_c(s,E)$. By step 2, $\operatorname{Fib}_s(g)=\gamma$. Hence $\operatorname{Fib}_s(u_{N'}f)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(gu_N)$, and faithfulness [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] gives $u_{N'}f=gu_N$. Since $J_s$ is $E$-linear and both termwise computations of step 3 are functorial in chain maps, $T^s_{E,\Omega}J_s(g)$ is $\gamma$'s matrix map through $E\to\Omega$. This is $\rho_{E,s}(\gamma)$ by the definition of $\rho_{E,s}$ on chain maps, so $\kappa_{P'}\circ T^s_{E,\Omega}J_s(g)=\rho_{E,s}(\varphi)\circ\kappa_P$. Conjugating by the diagonal rescalings of step 3 turns the lattice-basis matrices of $\varpi_E^r\gamma$ back into those of $\varpi_E^r\gamma$ in the original bases, and the scalar $\varpi_E^{-r}$ cancels $\varpi_E^r$. Combining with $\rho_{E,s}(\varphi)=\rho_{E,s}(c_{N'})\rho_{E,s}(\operatorname{Fib}_sf)\rho_{E,s}(c_N)^{-1}$ gives $\beta_{N'}\circ T^s_{E,\Omega}J_s(f)=\rho_{E,s}(\operatorname{Fib}_sf)\circ\beta_N$. A change of bases replaces the matrices by $D^{-1}AB$ on both sides, and [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace] states that $\rho_{E,s}$ is independent of bases through these change-of-basis isomorphisms. Thus $\beta$ is a specified natural isomorphism, independent of all choices.

source.place: First sentence, factorization over Q_l: basis independence and naturality of the point comparison

proof.text: Shifts and the unit. For $N[1]$ use the choices $C[1]$, $c_N[1]$, $P[1]$ and $u_N[1]$, which are allowed by step 4's independence. Here $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ commutes with shifts [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], and $Q(P)[1]=Q(P[1])$. Then $J_s$, $T^s_{E,\Omega}$ (both termwise here) and $\rho_{E,s}$ shift the identical finite free complex, with differential $-a^{i+1}$ in each case. So $\beta_{N[1]}=\beta_N[1]$. For the rational coefficient unit $E_s=A_s[0]$, take $C=E[0]$, $P=\mathcal O_E[0]$, $Q(P)=A_s[0]$ and $u_N=1$, since $\operatorname{Fib}_s(A_s)=\Gamma(s,A_s)\otimes E=E$ by step 2. Then $\kappa$ is $U_s\otimes_{E_s^c}(E_s^c\otimes_{A_s}A_s)\cong U_s$ by the multiplication maps, which is the canonical unit identification $T^s_{E,\Omega}J_s(E_s)\cong U_s=\rho_{E,s}(E[0])$ of [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace].

The delivery composed T∘J_s on D^b_c(s,E) without justifying this. The statement of lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization identifies the two categories over s, which is noetherian of dimension 0 with ell invertible: same completed sheaf and same morphisms, so the raw rationalizations are equal. I added one statement sentence citing it, plus three stmt_deps. The statement is clarified, not weakened. Fault 2 (C3/E4): step 2 treated Q(C) as a complex of E_s^c-modules and took its finite-free form from the proof of the point equivalence, not its statement. It now builds an integral lattice P by rescaling bases by varpi^{-mi}, and sets Q(P) = A_s^{rk} with the integral matrices, which lies in the category by condition (ii) of the characterization lemma. Gamma(s,A_s) = C(|s|,O_E) = O_E (lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction), so Fib_s(Q(P)) = C by def-weil-finite-coefficient-point. J is computed termwise on this K-flat complex; T^s is termwise by lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus; a diag(varpi^{-mi}) chain isomorphism returns the matrices of rho. Fault 3 (E5): naturality was asserted, not shown. It is now proved by lifting each derived map to a chain map (lem-pc-ring-derived-map-lift), clearing denominators, and using faithfulness of Fib_s; I checked the identity beta_{N'} TJ(f) = rho(Fib f) beta_N. I also checked: E_s^c (sfb and pbc constructions) is the same p_s^*C(-,E); U_s = Omega_s^c; rho's target is a full subcategory of D(Mod_{U_s}). Small cases tested: 0, E_s, E_s[-3], a contractible complex with varpi^{-2} differential, and multiplication by varpi^{-1}. Every proof dependency is on the sk-thm-rationality route.
